study.title: Psalm 31 Refuge, anguish, and confidence to the end
study.overview: Psalm 31 combines intense prayer, deep mourning and renewed confidence in the Lord. David presents himself as one surrounded by danger, shame, persecution and loneliness, but insists on trusting in the God of truth. Along the psalm, personal surrender unites to the remembrance of divine goodness: the Lord delivers, guards, hears, hides and strengthens. The final movement is community: whoever experiences the faithfulness of God calls other saints to love him and to wait for him with courage.

outline.title: Urgent request for free and confident delivery
outline.explanation: David begins supplicating that the Lord frees him without being ashamed. He asks immediate attention, protection as rock and strength, and claims to entrust his spirit in the hands of God, recognizing him as the God of truth and as the one who rescued him.

outline.title: Rejection of the emptiness and memory of the received kindness already received
outline.explanation: The psalmist departs from those who attach themselves to deceitful things and reaffirms his trust in the Lord. He celebrates the goodness of God, who saw his affliction, recognized the anguish of his soul, did not give him to the enemy and put him in a broad place, that is, in a safe and free space.

outline.title: I'm sorry for physical, social and spiritual pain
outline.explanation: From here the tone is of extreme distress: eyes, soul and body are consumed, the force failure and reputation has been attained among friends and acquaintances. There is fear around, conspiracy against his life and a sense of abandonment, but at the center of the crisis he still confesses: 'I trust you'. He asks the Lord to make his face shine, save it for his goodness and shut up his liar lips of the wicked.

outline.title: The goodness of God for those who fear him and the ultimate call to hope
outline.explanation: The psalm ends with adoration and encouragement. The goodness of God is presented as great and guarded to those who fear and trust in him; He hides them from arrogance and strife, hears when one feels cut off from before his eyes and answers supplication. Therefore, the saints are called to love the Lord, for he keeps the believers, repays the arrogant and strengthens the hearts of those who wait in him.

study.context: The notes only allow us to say that this psalm is attributed to David and that it may reflect a period of persecution, with suggested parallels to his escape from Saul. Matthew Henry considers it likely that it was written amid persecution, but acknowledges that the text does not inform with certainty occasion, place or date. Adam Clarke also notes that the psalm does not bring safe indications of time or place. Thus, the safest historical context is that of a righteous one pressed by enemies and the experience of near death, without fixing specific episodes as a fact confirmed by the chapter itself.
study.theology: The psalm teaches that faith and prayer walk together: trust in the Lord does not replace the cry, but deepens it. God is presented as a rock, stronghold, redeemer, God of truth and refuge for those who surrender to him. The language of the surrender of the spirit in his hands shows confidence in divine sovereignty over the time and outcome of life. The text also highlights that God's goodness is not abstract: it manifests itself in guarding, hiding, listening and strengthening those who fear and expect in him. At the same time, psalm does not soften the suffering of the righteous: there is bodily pain, public humiliation, social isolation and real threat. Theologically, this shows that trust in God can coexist with deep anguish, and that biblical hope does not deny the lamentation, but leads him to God. The community closure extends personal experience: whoever has been sustained by divine goodness calls others to love the Lord and persevere in hope.

scholarViews.insight: The psalmist presents his trust and his surrender to the Lord, and the commentary emphasizes that the Lord offers refuge to those who come to him for protection; this trust is also seen as a prefiguration of the suffering of Jesus.
The commentaries point out that faith and prayer walk together: whoever believes should pray, and the prayer of faith is effective. David, in anguish, asks for deliverance and divine support.

The commentary notes that the psalmist asks God to incline the ear, as those who spare immediate attention to an extreme situation; in addition, it compares the strong rock to natural fortifications used as shelter.

questions: What changes in prayer when I, like David, step from the mere description of the crisis to the explicit declaration of trust in God?
In which areas of my life do I still try to seek security in vain or deceitful things, rather than refuge in the Lord?
How can the memory of God's goodness strengthen my hope when I feel forgotten, humiliated or surrounded by pressure?
study.practice: Separate a time to make Psalm 31 his own prayer: describe before God his anguish with honesty, consciously given him his future, and end up praising him in a concrete way in which he has already sustained him. Then encourage another person afflicted with the words of verse 24: to remain waiting in the Lord is not passivity, but persevering confidence. In practice, this can mean renouncing today a false source of security, seeking reconciliation where there is confusion of words and reserving a moment to thank before asking for anything.
study.uncertainty: Notes do not allow you to safely identify the exact historical event, the location, or the date of the composition. Nor is it possible to conclusively affirm which verses should be read as a direct and intentional reference to Jesus; Tyndale's note treats this as a prefiguration, that is, Christian interpretation, not as a fact explicitly declared by the psalm. In addition, the poetic expressions about 'rocha', 'very strong house', 'wide place' and 'Xeol' were translated and explained in general, without pretense to exhaust their original literary force.
